output.summary: This amendment to a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Safe Passages changes the scope of work for in-person learning supports for students in grades 6-12 at Coliseum College Preparatory Academy. The term is August 1, 2020 through July 31, 2021, with no increase in cost.

output.headline: Pays Spanish Speaking Unity Council up to $200,000 for support of Latino male students and families
output.summary: The Spanish Speaking Unity Council would provide a coordinated system of academic and support services for Latino males and other students of color and their families, through the Office of Equity. The term is September 1, 2020 through May 28, 2021, for up to $200,000.00.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $4,500 for Elevate Oakland artists to mentor McClymonds High performing arts students
output.summary: 51Oakland, doing business as Elevate Oakland, provides professional artists who visit one to two times a week, by Zoom and in person when allowed, to share their careers with McClymonds High School students. output.summary: This amends the contract with Anthonio, Inc. for an inspector of record, who oversees construction work on the Emerson Elementary School Girls' Softball Field Project. It also extends the contract by 118 days, from December 3, 2020 to March 31, 2021.

output.headline: Ratifies a no-cost 2020-2023 agreement with Upward Roots for youth service learning at 15 schools
output.summary: Upward Roots, Inc. partners with schools and afterschool agencies to bring youth-led service learning to expanded learning programs at 15 schools. The Board is ratifying this memorandum of understanding (MOU) and COVID amendment, which began April 10, 2020 and runs to April 10, 2023, at no cost to the district.

output.headline: Approves a no-cost 2020-21 Soccer Without Borders program for newcomer students at seven schools
output.summary: Soccer Without Borders offers soccer practices and games combined with academic and language support, civic engagement and cultural exchange for newcomer students at seven schools. The agreement runs August 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021, at no cost to the district.

output.headline: Approves a no-cost 2020-2023 agreement with buildOn for high school community service learning
output.summary: buildOn would provide support and structured opportunities for high school students to do intensive community service learning, including international service learning projects. The agreement runs August 1, 2020 through August 1, 2023, at no cost to the district.

The Board is ratifying the agreement, which runs September 1, 2020 through August 31, 2023, at no cost to the district.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $60,000 for a contractor to coordinate volunteers for COVID food distribution
output.summary: An individual contractor would support food distribution during COVID by coordinating the volunteer process, supporting safety procedures and serving as a thought partner. The Board is ratifying the agreement, which began October 1, 2020 and runs through June 30, 2021, for up to $60,000.00.

output.summary: Ralph Bunche Academy asks to shift $10,000 of its 2020-2021 Measure N budget away from teacher salary stipends, which will cost less because of distance learning. The money would instead hire a consultant through the New Door Program to give students pre-employment training, job placement, case management and work skill training. This moves money within the school's budget and adds no new funds.

output.headline: Moves $1,500 at Ralph Bunche Academy from culinary equipment to audio-visual equipment
output.summary: Ralph Bunche Academy asks to shift $1,500 of its 2020-2021 Measure N budget away from culinary equipment, which will cost less because of distance learning. The money would instead buy audio-visual equipment to support student learning for career and college in the distance-learning model. This moves money within the school's budget and adds no new funds.

output.summary: Arbitrage Compliance Specialists, Inc. will help the district meet IRS arbitrage compliance requirements by reviewing documents on its debt issues, such as the Official Statement, Tax Certificate and IRS Form 8038-G. The work is for the Facilities Planning and Management Project and is set to run from July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2024. The agreement is for $12,750.

output.summary: Redgwick Construction Company, the lowest responsive bidder, would remove about 240 linear feet of concrete wall and the stairs to the playground and build a new retaining wall and stairs at Horace Mann Elementary School. output.summary: The district hires an environmental consulting firm to clear soil borings, drill for two days, remove waste from the drilling, sample the soil and write a report of its findings. output.summary: This amendment pays for continued private patrol security at The Center Project in November and December 2020. It raises the contract's not-to-exceed amount from $54,572.00 to $92,350.40.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $3,750 for Mills Teacher Scholars to support school leadership teams and teacher collaboration

output.summary: The Alameda County Registrar of Voters used Sequoia Elementary School as an accessible voting location from October 31 to November 3, 2020. The Registrar pays the district $200. The Board is approving the agreement after the voting dates.

output.summary: Refugee & Immigrant Transitions would provide remote services during distance learning, including English classes for up to 90 refugee adults, home-based tutoring for at least 20 refugee students, two community navigators, after-school tutoring at Fremont High and Oakland International High, and interpretation for district staff. output.summary: The Board is approving, after the fact, a contract with 51Oakland, doing business as Elevate Oakland, to give Parker Elementary students art and music programming. It runs from September 15, 2020 through June 30, 2021, at a cost of no more than $55,440.

output.headline: Pays Bay Area Community Resources up to $25,000 for a community manager at MLK Jr. and Lafayette

It runs from October 26, 2020 through May 28, 2021, at a cost of no more than $25,000.

output.summary: The district is hiring Bay Area Community Resources to give daily support to students with severe behavior and social-emotional challenges at Community United Elementary School. output.summary: This resolution gives the name Lockwood STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, Mathematics) Academy to the school created by merging Community United Elementary School and Futures Elementary School. output.summary: The district is accepting a $507,847 grant from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services to teach educators and staff to recognize and respond to signs of labor and sex trafficking. The grant also pays for age-appropriate lessons for students on how to avoid being victimized. It runs from September 30, 2020 through September 29, 2023.

output.summary: Curative Labs, Inc. will provide COVID-19 testing to screen certain district employees and contractors, at no cost to the district. The agreement runs from November 3, 2020 to November 3, 2023. The Board is approving it after the start date.

It runs July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2023, and the item does not state a dollar amount.

output.summary: Common Vision/Growing Together will support school gardens, including tree plantings, "Living Schoolyard" installations, general garden help, outdoor teaching training for staff and virtual home-based garden and cooking activities. It runs from November 2, 2020 through May 28, 2021, at a cost of no more than $200,000.
